verdicts.note: REVISES THE PRIOR ADJUDICATION, which read this as a forward-collision/AEB false-trigger using outside knowledge that a 2020 Rogue has standard AEB. Deciding from the text alone (no mention of ADAS, cameras, sensors, or warning messages -- just 'the breaks have locked up twice'): this is a literal brake complaint. Dropped FORWARD COLLISION AVOIDANCE entirely; kept as brake-family only because the subtype genuinely isn't stated (contrast 1837120/1886408, which explicitly describe sensor-triggered false braking with no obstacle and DO support FORWARD COLLISION AVOIDANCE).
Unlike 1779673 this one explicitly says the front and back sensors trigger for no reason, so FORWARD COLLISION AVOIDANCE is clearly right.
Stall/hesitation with no part named and no diagnosis -- both gpt-5.4 models chose UNKNOWN OR OTHER, which our own class definition supports. Same treatment as 1292185.
Mentions a hood support failure first, but the substantive complaint is the sticking gas pedal; no model chose STRUCTURE.
BORDERLINE: shifter stuck in park with the shifter assembly replaced and grounds tightened -- an electrical read is arguable, but the shift mechanism itself is drivetrain.

REVISES THE PRIOR ADJUDICATION, which accepted the old teacher's EQUIPMENT answer on the theory that gold was EQUIPMENT. Checked against the raw data directly: the true top-level COMPDESC for this row is 'ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING:COOLING SYSTEM', not EQUIPMENT -- the prior adjudication's note misstated the gold label. ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING is correct outright, no widening needed. Also resolves the B13 HVAC-routing question (see gotcha B13-revised): the heater CORE is physically part of the coolant loop, so heater-core complaints belong here regardless of whether defrost is mentioned.
Auto stop-start failing to restart the engine. All three models gave three different answers, which is itself a signal; ENGINE and ELECTRICAL SYSTEM (starter/battery) are both defensible.
A fractured subframe is structural even though the corroded wheel is mentioned alongside it.

All three models said STEERING and the dealer did diagnose the steering column, which houses the multifunction switch and clockspring. The symptoms (horn, turn signals, wipers) are electrical. Both are defensible.
Keeps the prior multi-issue call and adds the other brake subtypes, since the text gives no hydraulic/air/electric signal.
The entire narrative is 'THE BRAKES GRRIND.' No subtype is recoverable.
The water pump is explicitly named as failed, which is what distinguishes this from 1476775 where no coolant component was mentioned.

REVISES THE PRIOR ADJUDICATION, but narrower than the first pass here: checked against raw data, the true top-level COMPDESC is a clean 'VISIBILITY/WIPER' with no coolant-system coding at all, so ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING is dropped from accept (unlike 463855, no heater CORE is named here, only the blend/defrost symptom). NHTSA said VISIBILITY/WIPER, two models said VISIBILITY -- both accepted per the established B12 VISIBILITY-vs-VISIBILITY/WIPER noise pattern.

Rust on the rotors, pulling under braking. Our own SERVICE BRAKES, AIR definition literally says that class is used for 'ordinary hydraulic/disc brake complaints (rotors, calipers, ABS units)', so gpt-5.4-mini's answer follows the prompt as written.
CV joints are driveline, which POWER TRAIN's definition names explicitly; the SUSPENSION answers are model errors.
Not brake-family ambiguous: the text quotes '(Service Brakes, Hydraulic)' from the campaign.

CORRECTED after user pushback: I was widening this to be fair to models evaluated under an older, incomplete prompt -- but the truth doesn't change based on what a model happened to be told. Exhaust/catalytic converter complaints roll up to ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING at scale (~11k rows), confirmed against raw data. Single label. gpt-5-mini and gpt-5.4-mini's ENGINE answers are wrong (the prompt gap that caused this is fixed going forward, see gotcha B16, but that doesn't change what the correct label is today).
